The Atlantic Ocean is the second-largest ocean in the world, covering about 20% of Earth's surface.
Sea turtles in the Atlantic migrate thousands of miles across the ocean during their lifetime.
The Atlantic Ocean is home to the North Atlantic Gyre, which contains the infamous Sargasso Sea.
The deepest point in the Atlantic is the Puerto Rico Trench at about 27,480 feet deep.
Atlantic sea turtles can hold their breath for up to 7 hours while resting on the ocean floor.
The Gulf Stream, a warm ocean current in the Atlantic, is about 30 times larger than the Amazon River.
Over 3 million pieces of plastic enter the Atlantic Ocean every day.
Sea turtles have been swimming in Earth's oceans for over 100 million years.
Atlantic leatherback turtles can dive deeper than 4,000 feet below the surface.
The Atlantic contains about 20% of the world's fish species.
Sea turtles help maintain healthy seagrass beds by grazing on them, which benefits the entire ecosystem.
The Atlantic Ocean produces about half of the world's oxygen through phytoplankton.
Most sea turtles are endangered due to fishing nets, pollution, and habitat loss.
Atlantic sea turtles return to the same beaches where they were born to lay their own eggs.
Plastic bags are mistaken for jellyfish by sea turtles, which can be fatal if ingested.
